Jordan: quick heads-up: i sketched a tiered fallback + handshake flow for canary / A-B rollouts. need opinions on where decisions should be made (edge vs central) and how strict the runtime must be.
Mina: curious what you mean by 'handshake' here.
Jordan: runtime handshake = small synchronous check to ensure policy version + health token match before routing new-variant traffic. if mismatch -> safe-route. central policy does heavier judgement asynchronously.
Sanjay: runtime checks okay but keep them minimal. network calls in the hot path are dangerous under load.
Jordan: agreed. runtime only validates an opaque 64-bit policy-hash and a short TTL. central pushes signed deltas.
Ellie: what signals do you want at runtime? p99 latency, error spikes? or more?
Jordan: runtime: p95/p99, instant 5xx count over sliding 30s, instance oom, queue depth, and last-success timestamp for fallback chain. central: aggregated canary cohort metrics, offline evals (quality), customer tickets, downstream slow ops.
Priya: tenant sensitivity: we must let enterprise tenants have tighter thresholds. this needs to be in the policy blob.
Mina: policy blob idea: a small JSON map per route with severity bands named green/amber/red and actions enumerated. runtime interprets numeric thresholds + action enum.
Sanjay: enum actions? what granularity?
Mina: actions = {mirror:x, sample:y, route:variant_id, throttle_pct:z, hold} — keep it limited.
Jordan: propose priority order of triggers at central: quality regressions > correctness alerts > errors > latency > cost. runtime should only enforce errors and extreme latency.
Alex: soft diversion definition? I prefer 'stealth mirror' (mirror but do not count towards quota) + tiny sample live (0.5-1%). helps detect divergence without impacting customer bill.
Priya: logistically product needs an explicit pilot flag to opt specific tenants into the samples.
Ellie: we also need hysteresis to avoid flip-flop. suggest: require N windows above threshold to escalate; M windows below to relax; use exponential backoff for re-escalation.
Jordan: agreed. add a min-enforce-time to any escalation (e.g., 5 minutes) so we don't immediately bounce back.
Sanjay: how do we prevent policy skew across regions?
Mina: runtime nodes pull signed delta + version. on mismatch they report and enter safe-mode (route to golden) until policies reconcile. central keeps a last-known-good per-region stamp.
Alex: observability: every route decision must be tagged with policy_version, rule_id, decision_reason. keep a sample of counterfactuals (what would have happened).
Priya: costs: mirroring + sampling is expensive. policy should include a budget cap per tenant; if exceeded downgrade action.
Jordan: good. plan to include budget as numeric field in blob; central optimizer can recommend action downgrades when budget nears limit.
Ellie: session affinity concerns — when we divert mid-session, users might see inconsistent state. idea: sticky mapping with lease; on diversion, sticky key maps to fallback and keeps mapping for T minutes. add a 'soft_affinity' flag in policy.
Sanjay: fallback chains: runtime should attempt the ordered chain with quick health probes. if chain falls through, route to a stateless minimal model (golden) and emit high-severity alert.
Jordan: fallback chain health: store last N probe timestamps + success rate; if success_rate < threshold mark unhealthy. runtime uses these for decisioning.
Mina: DSL example snippet (kept tiny):
```
{"ver":3, "routes":{"/complete": {"bands":[{"name":"amber","p99":900,"action":"mirror:5,sample:1"},{"name":"red","p99":2000,"action":"route:fallback"}], "budget":100000}}}
```
Alex: keep the DSL minimal. no free-form scripting in fast-path.
Priya: console UX: expose presets (conservative, balanced, aggressive) and a raw JSON editor for infra customers. pilot mode toggle to pick tenants.
Ellie: rollout testing: CI sandbox that replays stored traffic and runs the policy engine offline to validate decisions + detect false positives.
Jordan: phase plan: 1) runtime evaluator + compact blob push, hard-fail rules; 2) central policy with per-tenant bands, console presets, pilot mode; 3) signal fusion (quality-weighted decisions), budget-aware optimizer, counterfactual capture.
Sanjay: runbook: when automatic fallback triggers unexpectedly, oncall runs `policy-diff` and `recent-decisions` and can force rollback via emergency policy tag. Alex?
Alex: i'll draft runbook commands and UI hooks to show policy diff + last 10 decisions + recent probe health.
Priya: also include customer-facing messaging templates for Product when an enterprise tenant is affected.
Jordan: todos: Mina/Sanjay prototype compact DSL + checksum; Ellie spec session-lease; Alex runbook + UI hooks; Priya templates + presets; Jordan will write RFC followup. sync next Wed 3pm.
ops-bot: reminder: architecture sync Wed 3:00pm in #architecture. :calendar:
Jordan: thanks everyone.
